summary.evaluation_methodology: Dual-pass extraction with deterministic rubric cross-check and portal ground-truth specification reproduction.

entries.agent_claim: gmail.modify is classified as a 'Sensitive Scope' requiring standard app review.
entries.ground_truth: gmail.modify is strictly classified as a 'Restricted Scope' under Google API Services User Data Policy, requiring Tier 2 CASA cyber security assessment.
entries.method: Verified against Google API Services User Data Policy specification and GCP Cloud Console Scopes reference table.
entries.impact: CRITICAL: Underestimating this would cause developers to budget 3 days for review instead of 4 weeks + $5,000 CASA security assessment fee.
entries.systematic_fix: Added explicit domain rule mapping mail.google.com and gmail.* scopes directly to Restricted severity.

entries.agent_claim: Review takes 3–5 business days according to developer docs.
entries.ground_truth: Slack developer docs state no SLA; community forums and actual developer submissions average 2 to 3 weeks for App Directory listing, while internal workspace installs are 0 seconds.
entries.method: Audited against official api.slack.com documentation and Slack App Directory distribution requirements.
entries.impact: HIGH: Clarified that development workspace requires 0 days, but external multi-tenant distribution takes weeks.
entries.systematic_fix: Split time estimates into 'setup_active_effort' vs 'approval_wait', and downgraded uncommitted wait claims to 'community-reported'.

entries.agent_claim: Requires approval before making OAuth app public to other GitHub users.
entries.ground_truth: Standard GitHub OAuth apps require NO approval whatsoever. Only GitHub Marketplace listings require review.
entries.method: Audited against GitHub Docs OAuth 2.0 application specification and verified multi-user authorization flow.
entries.impact: MEDIUM: Prevented false assumption of blocker. Baseline score confirmed at 0 (Easy).
entries.systematic_fix: Instructed researcher prompt to distinguish between OAuth Direct Authorization vs Marketplace/Directory listings.

entries.agent_claim: OAuth grant automatically exposes all pages and databases in the user's workspace.
entries.ground_truth: Notion enforces page-level isolation. Even with full content capabilities, the user must explicitly share specific pages with the integration.
entries.method: Verified against Notion Developers API reference on page-level permissions and OAuth access token capabilities.
entries.impact: HIGH: Prevents developers from writing buggy code that assumes root workspace access.
entries.systematic_fix: Added prominent Blocker & Fix for object_not_found.

entries.agent_claim: Developers can use the Free tier for creating automated agent posting bots.
entries.ground_truth: Free tier has a crippling global limit of 1,500 posts/month total per app and NO read/search access. Multi-user agents are blocked unless paying $100/mo Basic tier.
entries.method: Verified against developer.x.com portal pricing tables and modern v2 endpoint access tier limitations.
entries.impact: CRITICAL: Prevents surprise $100/mo bill and blocked MVP launches.
entries.systematic_fix: Difficulty rubric immediately assigns 'Gated' status if free tier lacks necessary read/write endpoints.

entries.agent_claim: PKCE is optional for Linear OAuth 2.0 web applications.
entries.ground_truth: Linear documentation and authorization endpoints require PKCE code_challenge and code_verifier for all authorization code flows.
entries.method: Audited against Linear API documentation for OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow with PKCE.
entries.impact: MEDIUM: Prevented authentication failures during token handshake.
entries.systematic_fix: Verifier pass flags any OAuth 2.0 flow lacking PKCE specification if modern RFC 7636 is enforced by provider.

entries.agent_claim: Requires Zoom Pro or Business paid account to create OAuth apps.
entries.ground_truth: Zoom allows free basic accounts to create 'General App' OAuth integrations in developer marketplace.
entries.method: Audited against Zoom App Marketplace documentation for General and Server-to-Server OAuth apps.

entries.agent_claim: Asana access tokens expire in 1 hour and provide permanent refresh tokens.
entries.ground_truth: Asana access tokens expire in 3,600 seconds (1 hour); refresh tokens do not expire unless explicitly revoked or dormant for 60+ days.
entries.method: Audited against Asana OAuth 2.0 authentication guide for access token expiration (3,600s) and refresh token mechanics.

entries.agent_claim: Apps with less than 50 users can remain in 'Development' status indefinitely without review.
entries.ground_truth: Dropbox Developer portal allows up to 500 connected users for development status before requiring 'Production' review.
entries.method: Audited against Dropbox Developers App Console documentation regarding 500-user limit before Production status.
entries.impact: MEDIUM: Agent hallucinated legacy 50-user threshold from old API v1 forum post instead of current API v2 docs.
entries.systematic_fix: Prompt verifier enforces date-check on forum references and penalizes unverified quota assertions.

unfamiliar_app_tests.accuracy_notes: Correctly identified User-managed vs Admin-managed app types; noted Marketplace review is needed only for public publishing.
Correctly identified instant self-serve OAuth app registration; accurately captured Bearer token rotation.
Sourced correct OAuth endpoints, but initially hallucinated 50 user limit from outdated blog; verifier pass flagged and updated to 500.
